newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down on slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down on slow trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed marginally down on Monday on what traders said was a lackluster session due to the absence of U.S. investors rather than any market trend, traders said.
"It was very, very slow. Volume was thin, and even today's meager total included cross trades," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended off 3.27 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,985.02.
Trading volume was razor thin at 26.97 million shares.
U.S. financial markets were closed for Memorial Day.
Dealers said dealing slowed further as open outcry was replaced for the day by a screen trading system called SENTRA.
"The market was very apathetic. Very little happened and when you use SENTRA, volume always falls," another desk trader said.
Traders said several stocks moved on recent news or press reports.
"Ece and Cifra gained, CIE fell and that was about all that happened," a desk trader said.
Restaurant chain Ece gained 68 centavos to 11.40 pesos following an announcement late on Friday by the Interior Ministry the firm had jointly won a concession to run Mexico City's racecourse.
Entertainment firm Compania Interamericana de Entretenimiento meanwhile fell due to failing to win the same concession, traders said.

Retail chain Cifra gained 60 centavos to 13.30 pesos after a business column in El Financiero newspaper, which cited no source, said a deal was forthcoming to sell some holdings to Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
A Cifra spokesman was not immediately available for comment. No one was immediately available for comment at Wal-Mart's headquarters in Bentonville, Ark.
Cifra's C class shares also gained, ending up 56 centavos to 12.74 pesos.
"The spread between Cifra's B and C shares was so wide it lent itself to switching," a trader said.
Cifra B and C shares together accounted for about one-fifth of all shares traded.
On the broad market, 105 shares changed hands, of which sliders outnumbered gainers by 41 to 29.
